reason: The cited evidence does not address Al substitution in HfMoTaTiZr or any Hf-containing RHEA. E1 discusses subtraction of elements from HfMoNbTaTiZr but does not mention Al or density reduction. E2 shows Al reduces density in a different alloy system (Al-Nb-Ti-V) but provides no support for Al effects on phase stability, strengthening, or high-temperature properties in Hf-based alloys. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Al substitution for Hf reduces density due to lower atomic mass
Al can promote solid-solution and/or precipitation strengthening in RHEAs
The modified alloy retains a predominantly single-phase or fine-precipitate microstructure
Microstructure and properties remain stable up to ~1000 °C
Strength and ductility are preserved at room and elevated temperatures
